definitions.explanation: A hairless, thick-bodied caterpillar, typically of a moth or butterfly. The word specifically refers to the plump, smooth type (not hairy caterpillars, which are called 毛虫). Originally named for caterpillars found on sweet potato plants.

examples.japanese: ⟦{葉|は}っぱ→葉っぱ：05388_happa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{芋虫|いもむし}がいた。
examples.english: There was a caterpillar on a leaf.

examples.japanese: {芋虫|いもむし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦やがて→やがて：03637_yagate⟧⟦{蝶|ちょう}→蝶：04288_chou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: A caterpillar eventually becomes a butterfly.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦キャベツ→キャベツ：05187_kyabetsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}たら→見る：00283_miru⟧、{芋虫|いもむし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧ついて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: When I looked at the cabbages in the garden, there were a lot of caterpillars on them.

notes:
USAGE:
{芋虫|いもむし} refers specifically to smooth, hairless caterpillars. Hairy caterpillars are called ⟦{毛虫|けむし}→毛虫：04933_kemushi⟧. The name comes from ⟦{芋|いも}→芋：10231_imo⟧ (sweet potato/taro) + ⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧ (insect), as these caterpillars were commonly found on potato plants.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {芋虫|いもむし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{這|は}う→這う：00094_hau⟧: a caterpillar crawls
- {芋虫|いもむし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{蛹|さなぎ}→蛹：21225_sanagi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: a caterpillar becomes a chrysalis
- ⟦{青|あお}い→青い：00586_aoi⟧{芋虫|いもむし}: a green caterpillar
